title: The light in the hall

item.name: The light in the hall
item.line: A small light that moves about the locked hall after 11 at night, stops by the piano for an hour, and goes out before midnight.

brief: The minute book for 2011 is in the hall safe, ribbon uncut. And for 3 nights now the hall has not been empty after dark.
From the street a small light moves about the locked hall after 11, stops at the far end for an hour, and goes out.
The street has decided the hall is haunted. The caretaker has decided it is not. Somebody has to go in and look.
4 people could have been in there. What is it, really?

suspects.name: Mr Cole
suspects.line: Locks the hall every night at 10.30. Says no ghost gets past his keys.
suspects.says: I locked up and went home. Ask my sister.

suspects.name: Theo
suspects.line: Back in the street's good books. Out late with his camera, and he saw the light too.
suspects.says: I was outside, taking pictures of it. That is how I know it is real.

suspects.name: Otto
suspects.line: The piano is the choir's. He says somebody has moved his music.
suspects.says: I have not touched that piano since Sunday.

suspects.name: Ines
suspects.line: Keeps the door at every event in the hall. Took the last bus home all week.
suspects.says: I go home after the 10.30 round. I have nothing to do with ghosts.

steps.fact: Nobody walks through walls with a torch. Somebody came in at the side door in muddy shoes, lit a candle, sat with their back to the window and went to the piano. A key with no tag was left under a chair.
steps.lead: A key with no tag is a key nobody signed for. The caretaker's key book says which keys are signed out.

steps.thing: The key book, and the ticket roll from the bus to the next town. Mr Cole keeps the first, and the bus company keeps the second.
steps.fact: Every signed key is on its hook. Mr Cole's own ring went with him on the 10.45 to his sister's, all 3 nights, and came back on the first bus.
steps.lead: Not Mr Cole, then, and not a signed key. The watchman logs the row each night, and 1 line is missing from each.

steps.thing: The watchman's log for last night, with a gap in it.

events: 10.30 pm. The round: every light off, every door locked.
11 pm. A light crosses from the side door to the piano, and stays an hour.
11.10 pm. Theo stops in the street and photographs the window.

options.text: Theo lets himself in at the front and walks round with his lamp.
Somebody lets themselves in at the side door with a key of their own.
A light left burning from the evening is knocked over by a draught.

steps.fact: Somebody let themselves in at the side door with their own key, after the round. Theo was in the street with his camera, and has never held a key to the hall.
steps.pin: In at the side door, 11 pm
steps.lead: Who goes to a piano at 11 at night? Otto says somebody moved his music. The choir's bookings are blotted on his desk.

steps.thing: The choir's booking blotter. The bookings went to the printer, but the blotter kept the ink, back to front.

steps.fact: The choir sang at a wedding in Oakfield from Friday to Sunday, and Otto went with it. He was 2 hours away on all 3 nights.
steps.lead: 4 finds in 4 places. Walk the hall once more, door to piano, before anybody is named.

steps.thing: The case, walked once more from the side door. Each find goes back where it was found.
steps.fact: On the piano's stand is a beginner's book, marked in pencil up to page 40, and a card tucked in it: "For Mum, 80 on Saturday."
steps.lead: A key nobody signed for, an hour at the piano, and a song for somebody's mother. 3 accounts are going round the street.

steps.thing: 3 accounts of the light in the hall. Each piece of evidence already on the board strikes 1 of them out.

accounts.text: The hall is haunted, as the street says.
Somebody with a key of their own comes at night to learn the piano in secret.
Theo stages the light for his photographs.

steps.fact: Chance: in at the side door after the 10.30 round. Means: a key nobody signed for. Motive: a song for a mother's 80th.

ending.found: It is Ines, at the piano at 11 at night, by torchlight, with a beginner's book open at page 41. She had stopped taking the last bus home.
ending.confession: My mother turns 80 on Saturday, and she has asked for 1 song all her life. I wanted to play it for her in the hall where she was married.
ending.after: The committee lets her practise on Thursdays, with the lights on. Nobody signed her key out: it came in an envelope with no name on it, with the lantern card.
